mia: Heads up — hitting an OOM on gcp-rt-37 during a long-chat run. kernel-picker + kvcache reuse enabled. looked like KV kept growing and never yielded.

devon: Which workload? long context or bursty batching? any repro id?

mia: longctx ~120k tokens, mixed small batches + streaming, reuse=true, kernel policy = auto-select+perf-stable. repro id: run/2026-03-17-rtgcp37.

anya: I remember a similar spike but that was due to compaction worker being starved during heavy memcpy. Could be different but worth profiling.

mia: Paste from runtime logs and OOM killer snippet: ```
[oom_reaper] task: inference-worker pid 8423 killed oom-killer: allocation failed, dev=0x3 
kvcache: alloc 1834219520 -> total_cache 5.8GB -> soft_reserve 6.0GB -> no eviction triggered
stack: runtime::kv::alloc_prefix+0x1a3
```

sam: can you also dump kv slab stats / paging counters? need kvcache.page_faults, evict_count, reuse_hits.

mia: slab stats: `slab_total=6144MB, slab_used=5420MB, slab_frag=12%, slab_reuse=74%, page_faults=1123, evict_count=4, async_compact_paused=true`

devon: interesting — evict_count is very low given page_faults. Looks like shadow pool overcommit: we reserve extra space for reuse but disable preemptive eviction when kernel=perf-optimized. allocation kept growing until OOM.

anya: yep. perf counters showed long periods where compaction loop scheduled but skipped (worker yield) while memcpy hot path held locks. kernel selection chosen an attention-kernel that spikes memcpy. bad interaction.

mia: attached minimal perf output: ```
perf top: memcpy 42%, kv_alloc 18%, compaction_yield 3%
flame: kv_alloc -> memcpy -> wait_on_compact
```

devon: mitigation plan (short): 1) reduce kvcache.soft_overcommit to 1.05x (or set `kvcache.max_prefix_bytes=1g`) 2) force fallback kernel to fallback-quant for canary nodes so compaction path isn't starved 3) enable forced eviction when async_compact_paused=true. I'll push a hotfix.

eng-sre-bot: devon deployed canary patch to gcp-rt-37: kvcache.max_prefix_bytes=1g, kernel_fallback=fallback-quant. rollout=canary(1/3). :rocket:

anya: Also recommend graceful degrade pattern so user requests aren't dropped: when mem > threshold -> mark request as degraded, trigger prefix eviction + async spill to disk and schedule a single retry with backoff. Pseudocode: ```
if (mem_used > threshold) {
  evict_prefix(n=1);
  spawn(async_spill(current_prefix));
  return RETRY_WITH_SHORTER_CTX;
}
```

mia: patched canary is running. after ~30m we saw allocation growth stop. no new OOMs for 2 hours on canary. p99 latency +20ms, cost delta negligible.

devon: follow-ups: emit telemetry `kvcache.eviction_forced`, `kvcache.shadow_overcommit_trigger`, and add dashboard alerts when forced_evictions > 5/min. Also add a unit test that simulates memcpy-heavy kernel + paused compaction.

sam: I'll open a reproducible test harness and file GH issue (internal) with traces and perf data — assigning myself. will link as #4392.

mia: Thanks all. leaving canary running, will roll to rest of pool if stable for 6h. :thumbsup:
